docRequirement: mcp-quickstart.md:333 binds the MCP server startup timeout to a 30-second default that an operator raises with the `MCP_TIMEOUT` environment variable, in milliseconds — the page gives `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000 claude` (:336) and `$env:MCP_TIMEOUT = "60000"; claude` (:342) as the remedy for "Connection timed out at startup". env-vars.md:410 restates it: "`MCP_TIMEOUT` | Timeout in milliseconds for MCP server startup (default: 30000, or 30 seconds)", and env-vars.md:406 marks it explicitly "Distinct from `MCP_TIMEOUT`, which bounds an individual server's connect attempt" when describing the separate `MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5000 ms blocking-startup batch wait).
current: The deadline exists with the documented default but has no operator lever. `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:205` declares `const MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;` documented as the "Per-server connect deadline" (:200-204). `mcp-pool.ts:689` resolves it as `this.connectTimeoutMs = Math.max(1, options?.connectTimeoutMs ?? MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS);` — the only override is the programmatic `connectTimeoutMs` constructor option declared at `mcp-pool.ts:653`. It is applied in `connectWithDeadline` (`mcp-pool.ts:1189-1206`), which races `connectWithRetries` against a single `setTimeout(this.connectTimeoutMs)` and rejects with `Timeout: "<slug>" did not connect within 30000ms` (:1196). The rejection is caught in the reconcile pass at `mcp-pool.ts:1509-1513`, which pushes the slug onto `failures` and adds it to `failedConnections`; `failedSlugsForLeaser` (:1651-1660) is what reports it to the leasing session. There is exactly ONE production construction of the pool — `defaultCreatePool` at `packages/server-core/src/mcp/workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:786-805` — and it passes only `workspaceRootPath`, `debug`, `pluginProcessAuthority`, `toolDescriptorStore` and `retry: MCP_CONNECT_RETRY` (:790-803); it does NOT pass `connectTimeoutMs`, so 30 s is fixed in every shipped path. `grep -rna "MCP_TIMEOUT"` over source (NUL-safe, excluding node_modules/dist/.references) returns zero hits outside docs, and no `NESSY_`-prefixed connect-timeout reader exists either. Positive control for that absence: the same module DOES read a Nessy-prefixed MCP env override — `process.env.NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` at `mcp-pool.ts:1959-1960` — so the same grep would have found a connect-timeout reader. Two near-misses are NOT this lever: a per-server `timeout` in `.mcp.json` is mapped to `toolTimeoutMs` (tool execution) at `packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:96-99`, and the `timeout?: number` defaulting to 30000 at `packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:226` / `:317` belongs to `validateStdioMcpConnection`, the config test-connection path, not the runtime pool.
divergence: The VALUE is right and the SEMANTICS are right — our 30 s is Claude's `MCP_TIMEOUT` default with Claude's meaning (bounds one server's connect). What is missing is only the operator lever: no environment variable of any spelling reaches `connectTimeoutMs`, so `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000` is silently inert and the documented remedy for a slow first `npx` download cannot be applied. Two second-order deltas ride along. (a) Name collision: our module constant is spelled `MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`, which is a REAL but DIFFERENT Claude env var (env-vars.md:406, default 5000, the blocking-startup batch wait) — exposing our constant under its current name would ship a var whose name means something else upstream. (b) Budget shape: Claude's `MCP_TIMEOUT` "bounds an individual server's connect attempt", whereas our 3-attempt initial-connect retry (`MCP_CONNECT_RETRY = { attempts: 3, baseDelayMs: 250 }`, workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:784) runs INSIDE the one 30 s deadline (mcp-pool.ts:1202 races `connectWithRetries` against the deadline), so all attempts share the budget.

change.what: Add the env lever. Introduce a module-local reader next to the constant, e.g. `function mcpStartupTimeoutMsFromEnv(env = process.env): number | undefined { const raw = (env.NESSY_MCP_TIMEOUT ?? '').trim(); if (!raw) return undefined; const value = Number(raw); return Number.isInteger(value) && value > 0 ? value : undefined; }` — trim, empty/malformed/non-positive falls back silently, matching `mcpAutoBackgroundDelayMs` at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:118-122. Then change :689 to `this.connectTimeoutMs = Math.max(1, options?.connectTimeoutMs ?? mcpStartupTimeoutMsFromEnv() ?? MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS);`. Precedence matters: the programmatic option MUST still win, because it is the focused-test seam that ~13 test call sites pass; env only replaces the compile-time default. Read `process.env` at construction (not per connect) so the pool's deadline is stable for its lifetime, matching how `connectTimeoutMs` is used today. Name: `NESSY_MCP_TIMEOUT`, following this repo's documented rebrand mapping (`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS` → `NESSY_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS`, background-task-settings.ts:10; `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` → `NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, mcp-pool.ts:237). Roughly 8 lines.

Recommended in the same edit: rename the constant to `MCP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` (module-private; three references — the declaration :205, the `{@link}` in the constructor option docblock :651, and the fallback :689). Its current spelling is Claude's OTHER env var (env-vars.md:406, default 5000, blocking-startup batch wait), and the phase1 row on `MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING`/`MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` is still open — leaving the name occupied guarantees a collision when that row is built. Pure rename, no behaviour change.

Add three cases against the existing `HangingPool` (:18): (1) positive — with `process.env.NESSY_MCP_TIMEOUT` set to a raised value and NO `connectTimeoutMs` option, the pool's deadline is the env value (assert via elapsed time on a hanging connect, or expose the resolved deadline through the existing timeout message text `did not connect within <n>ms`); (2) negative — a malformed value (`'soon'`, `'-5'`, `'0'`) falls back to the 30 s default; (3) precedence — an explicit `connectTimeoutMs` option still wins over a set env var. Save/restore `process.env.NESSY_MCP_TIMEOUT` in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` exactly as `packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-pool-call-idle-timeout.test.ts:34-39` does for `NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`; leaking it would perturb the ~26 other pool suites.

blastRadius: Process-env boundary only — nothing crosses a wire, schema or persistence boundary, and the value is never serialized, so this is NOT a repo risk trigger. Readers of the changed line: `McpClientPool` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:641-695) is the single constructor; the one production construction is `defaultCreatePool` (packages/server-core/src/mcp/workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:786), owned by `WorkspaceMcpPoolRegistry` (workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:171), which `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2226` holds and 9 call sites in that file lease from; `PiAgent` reads the leased pool through `config.mcpPool` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:941) and `packages/shared/src/mcp/pool-server.ts:67` wraps it. The env must be present in the process that OWNS the pool — the Electron main process and `bin/nessy-server` — not in the Pi subprocess; no subprocess env plumbing is involved. Test blast radius is the real cost: ~26 test subclasses extend `McpClientPool`, and 13 call sites already pass `connectTimeoutMs` explicitly (mcp-pool-connect-deadline.test.ts:40,49,77; mcp-pool-connect-retry.test.ts:50,60,73,89,113,135; mcp-pool-connect-on-demand.test.ts:78,108,124,180) — the option-wins precedence keeps every one of them env-insensitive, which is why that ordering is not optional. The optional constant rename touches only mcp-pool.ts:205,651,689 (module-private, no export). Gate: `bun run typecheck:shared` plus the four `packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-pool-connect-*.test.ts` suites; run them serially, since concurrent `bun test` processes manufacture failures in env-mutating suites.
userImpact: Observable, and it hits the exact scenario the page's troubleshooting accordion is written for. A user adds a stdio MCP source whose first launch cold-downloads its package (`npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest` and similar) and needs more than 30 s: the connect is abandoned at the deadline (mcp-pool.ts:1196), the reconcile records the slug as failed (mcp-pool.ts:1509-1513) and reports it through `failedSlugsForLeaser` (:1651), so the source shows as failed in Sources and its tools are absent from that turn. The user then does what the Claude troubleshooting page tells them to do — set `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000` — and nothing changes, with no message explaining why, because no code reads it. There is no per-server escape either: a `timeout` field in `.mcp.json` is routed to tool-execution time (project-config.ts:98), not startup. In practice the source recovers on a later sync once the package cache is warm (mcp-pool.ts:1505 retries connects for slugs without a live client), so the damage is repeated startup failures and an unusable documented remedy rather than a permanent outage. Users on fast networks with warm caches never see it.

Two things I did NOT verify and deliberately left out of the change list. (1) Whether the abandoned stdio child is killed at the deadline or left running to finish its download — I did not read the transport teardown path, so the userImpact text says the attempt is abandoned and retried on the next sync rather than claiming anything about the partial npx cache. (2) The retry-budget delta (b) is left as a recorded deviation, not a fix: making each of the 3 attempts get its own deadline would let one hung server hold ~90 s, and workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:799-803 says the shared bound is deliberate ('bounded by the pool's ONE connect deadline'). Changing it is an owner decision, not a doc-conformance repair; the env lever alone makes the documented remedy work.
